confidence_notes: Two web searches were used: one for the RBA rate and one for food and drink prices. The food and drink anchors start from crowd-sourced cost-of-living figures from MyLifeElsewhere (https://www.mylifeelsewhere.com/cost-of-living/punta-cana-c8115) and TravelTables (https://traveltables.com/country/dominican-republic/city/punta-cana/cost-of-living, last updated July 2023). Those sites show a domestic beer at about USD 2.4-2.6, a cappuccino at about USD 1.7-2.4 and an inexpensive meal at about USD 7-8 (range about USD 5.6-16). These figures are mostly local prices and may be out of date. I raised them for tourist-area venues in the Bavaro/Punta Cana zone and for price levels in July 2026, but did not check that adjustment against a source. The searches gave no direct figures for the mid-range meal, cocktails or wine. I estimated the mid-range meal from typical Caribbean resort-area restaurant prices. I estimated cocktails and wine from their usual local price relationship to beer, at about 2.5 times the beer price. All accommodation anchors come from general knowledge, not live listings, and are the least certain. Registered hostels are scarce in Punta Cana, so the dorm and private hostel figures are especially uncertain. Many visitors stay in all-inclusive resorts, which pushes up prices for standard 3-star rooms.
comparable_city_reasoning: The anchors combine crowd-sourced Punta Cana cost-of-living data with an uplift for resort-area prices. For comparison I used Caribbean and Latin American beach-resort cities with similar tourism demand, such as Playa del Carmen. Local Dominican price levels set the lower bound.
